properties.areaDesc: San Diego County Coastal Areas; Orange County Coastal
properties.headline: Coastal Flood Warning issued October 11 at 3:53AM PDT until October 11 at 3:00PM PDT by NWS San Diego CA
properties.description:
* WHAT...For the Coastal Flood Warning through Sunday afternoon,
significant coastal flooding and beach erosion is likely. For
the Beach Hazards Statement from Sunday morning until Sunday
evening, surf of 5 to 7 feet with local sets up to 9 feet. For
the Coastal Flood Advisory from Sunday afternoon until Tuesday
afternoon, minor coastal flooding expected.

* WHERE...San Diego County Coastal Areas and Orange County
Coastal Areas.

* WHEN...For the Coastal Flood Warning, until 3 PM PDT Sunday.
For the Beach Hazards Statement, from Sunday morning through
Sunday evening. For the Coastal Flood Advisory, from 3 PM
Sunday to 2 PM PDT Tuesday.

* IMPACTS...Numerous roads and beach boardwalks may be closed
due to high water. Low-lying property including homes,
businesses, and some critical infrastructure may flood during
morning high tides. Beach erosion. Elevated surf will lead to
a high risk of rip currents and dangerous swimming conditions.

* ADDITIONAL DETAILS...Greatest impacts on this morning from Post-Tropical
Cyclone Rachel with a combination of increased swell, onshore
winds, and high tides locally over 7.5 feet. High tides lower
each day into the middle of the week.
properties.instruction:
Take the necessary actions to protect flood-prone property. If
travel is required, do not drive around barricades or through
water of unknown depth.

Remain out of the water to avoid hazardous swimming conditions.

* WHERE...San Diego County Coastal Areas and Orange County
Coastal Areas.

* WHEN...For the Coastal Flood Warning, until 3 PM PDT Sunday.
For the Beach Hazards Statement, from Sunday morning through
Sunday evening. For the Coastal Flood Advisory, from 3 PM
Sunday to 2 PM PDT Tuesday.

* IMPACTS...Numerous roads and beach boardwalks may be closed
due to high water. Low-lying property including homes,
businesses, and some critical infrastructure may flood during
morning high tides. Beach erosion. Elevated surf will lead to
a high risk of rip currents and dangerous swimming conditions.

* ADDITIONAL DETAILS...Greatest impacts on this morning from Post-Tropical
Cyclone Rachel with a combination of increased swell, onshore
winds, and high tides locally over 7.5 feet. High tides lower
each day into the middle of the week.

properties.headline: Flood Watch issued October 11 at 6:44AM EDT until October 11 at 8:00PM EDT by NWS Blacksburg VA
properties.description:
* WHAT...Flooding caused by excessive rainfall continues to be
possible.

* WHERE...Portions of North Carolina, including the following areas,
Alleghany NC, Ashe, Surry, Watauga and Wilkes and southwest
Virginia, including the following areas, Carroll, Floyd, Grayson
and Patrick.

* WHEN...Through this evening.

* IMPACTS...Excessive runoff may result in flooding of rivers,
creeks, streams, and other low-lying and flood-prone locations.
Creeks and streams may rise out of their banks. Low-water crossings
may be flooded. Storm drains and ditches may become clogged with
debris.

* ADDITIONAL DETAILS...
- As the remnants of Isaias move northward into the lower Ohio
Valley, periods of rain will continue. Heavier rainfall will
continue in short bursts through the day. Additional rainfall
amounts of 1 to 3 inches, along with what has already fallen will
keep the threat of flooding around.
- http://www.weather.gov/safety/flood
properties.instruction:
You should monitor later forecasts and be alert for possible Flood
Warnings. Those living in areas prone to flooding should be prepared
to take action should flooding develop.

properties.areaDesc: Rutherford, NC
properties.headline: Flash Flood Warning issued October 11 at 6:40AM EDT until October 11 at 8:45AM EDT by NWS Greenville-Spartanburg SC
properties.description:
FFWGSP

The National Weather Service in Greenville-Spartanburg has extended
the

* Flash Flood Warning for...
Rutherford County in western North Carolina...

* Until 845 AM EDT.

* At 640 AM EDT, Doppler radar indicated thunderstorms continuing to
produce heavy rain across the warned area. Between 3 and 5 inches
of rain have fallen, with additional torrential rainfall moving
through eastern Rutherford County.  Flash flooding is ongoing.
High flows should be expected on area creeks and streams, including
along Cleghorn Creek in Rutherfordton, Floyds Creek near Forest
City, and Mountain Creek near Green Hill.

HAZARD...Flash flooding caused by heavy rain.

SOURCE...Radar indicated.

IMPACT...Expect flash flooding of low-lying areas near streams,
including  parks, trails, low-water crossings, boat-
access areas, and  campgrounds.  Significant flooding of
poor-drainage areas are likely, impacting travel.
Low-lying roadways are likely to be flooded, requiring
barricades.

* Some locations that will continue to experience flash flooding
include...
Forest City, Rutherfordton, Spindale, Ellenboro, Bostic, South
Mountains State Park, Alexander Mills, Sunshine, Union Mills and
Caroleen.
properties.instruction:
Be especially cautious at night when it is harder to recognize the
dangers of flooding.

Be aware of your surroundings and do not drive on flooded roads.

properties.areaDesc: Cherokee, SC
properties.headline: Flood Advisory issued October 11 at 6:36AM EDT until October 11 at 8:45AM EDT by NWS Greenville-Spartanburg SC
properties.description:
* WHAT...Flooding caused by excessive rainfall continues.

* WHERE...Cherokee County in upstate South Carolina...

* WHEN...Until 845 AM EDT.

* IMPACTS...Nuisance flooding of low-lying areas adjacent to streams
and other poor-drainage areas, including farmland, parks,
greenways, boat-access areas, golf courses, underpasses, and
parking lots. Isolated, shallow flows over roadways is possible. A
few flood-prone, low-water crossings may become impassible. A small
culvert washout or two is possible.

* ADDITIONAL DETAILS...
- At 631 AM EDT, Doppler radar indicated torrential rainfall has
entered eastern Cherokee County, with additional 1-2" possible
over the next hour.  This rainfall is occurring on top of
saturated soils due to a prolonged period of light to moderate
showers that have occurred over the county since yesterday
morning. Widespread, storm-total rainfall of the 2.5-3.5 inches
fell yesterday. The rainfall has accumulated steadily, allowing
soils to slowly saturate and runoff to slowly increase, resulting
in steady rises in small streams. However, this brief period of
torrential rainfall may cause more rapid rises to develop,
especially near Chesnee in the headwaters of Thicketty Creek,
Zekial Creek, Little Horse Creek, and Suck Creek as well as in
city of Gaffney at the headwaters of Peoples Creek, Limestone
Creek, and Irene Creek.  Isolated out-of-bank conditions
impacting low-lying areas adjacent to streams are likely
occurring.

- Some locations that will experience flooding include...
Gaffney, Cowpens, Blacksburg, Pacolet Mills, Grover, Cowpens
National Battlefield, Kings Mountain State Park, Crowders
Mountain State Park, Draytonville and Cherokee Falls.
- http://www.weather.gov/safety/flood
properties.instruction:
Be especially cautious at night when it is harder to recognize the
dangers of flooding.

Be aware of your surroundings and do not drive on flooded roads.

* WHERE...West Central San Diego County in southwestern California...

* WHEN...Until 530 AM PDT.

* IMPACTS...Minor flooding in low-lying and poor drainage areas.

properties.description:
A Marine Weather Statement has been issued for the following areas...
Sebastian Inlet to Jupiter Inlet 0-20 nm...
Sebastian Inlet to Jupiter Inlet 20-60 nm...
Volusia-Brevard County Line to Sebastian Inlet 0-20 nm...
Volusia-Brevard County Line to Sebastian Inlet 20-60 nm...

At 629 AM EDT, Doppler radar indicated a band of strong
thunderstorms, capable of producing winds to around 30 knots,
extending from just offshore the Treasure coast northward to well
offshore the Brevard coast. Cell motion was north at 20 knots.
properties.instruction:
Mariners can expect gusty winds to around 30 knots, locally higher
waves, and lightning strikes. Boaters should seek safe harbor
immediately until this storm passes.

Frequent cloud to water lightning is occurring with some of these
storme. If caught on the open water stay below deck and, if
possible, avoid ungrounded metal objects. Remember, lightning can
strike beyond 10 miles away from a thunderstorm.
